strings.rmbody: The Living Arkham is the web edition —interactive and available in several languages— of The Arkham Grimoire, FFG's official rules-clarification compendium for Arkham Horror: The Card Game, and of the FAQ chapter 1 (the pre-2026 notes, errata and frequently asked questions). It's a free tool created by Rincón Miskatonic, a Spanish blog about tabletop-gaming content, where you'll find scenarios, guides, resources and more free material for the game. Beyond reproducing these documents interactively, it also offers extra tools to help and expand the game.

strings.tbbleedintro: A print bleed is a few extra millimetres of art around the card, for presses that cut many at once and may drift slightly. Printing at home usually doesn't need it.
strings.tbnobleedsub: The card's final size, cut right on the edge.
strings.tbwithbleedsub: Adds ~3 mm of art on every side for a flush trim.
strings.tbintro: The taboo list re-tunes the experience cost or the text of certain cards to keep play balanced. Here is every affected card, as printed and as the taboo changes it.
strings.tbfaqnote: These are the taboos from the list published on 19 February 2026 (FAQ 2.5). More may be published in the future.
strings.tbbeta: This section isn't available in your language yet — the taboo cards are shown in English. It's in beta; report anything wrong to Rincón Miskatonic.
strings.tbforbiddenrule: Cannot be included in a deck.
strings.tbfrontsame: This card's taboo does not change the face: the taboo face is the printed card. The change is on the back.
strings.tbnoteline: The taboo does not rewrite this card: it only changes its experience cost, or forbids it. The taboo face is the printed card with the list line on it — which is exactly what FFG reprints.
strings.tbdisclaimer: The full text is not available on ArkhamDB, nor has FFG released it in your language for this card. The taboo face is the printed card with the text changed by the Rincón Miskatonic team. Some translations (especially outside Spanish) were done with the help of a machine translator. Please review the content before printing the cards in this section and, if you spot any mistake, contact Rincón Miskatonic so it can be fixed. Thank you very much.

strings.ubintro: Ultimatums are rules that make the game harder for a group of investigators; Boons, conversely, make it easier. Browse them here card by card. The text is taken from the Grimoire’s {opt} chapter (chapter 2) and, for the chapter-1 refractions, from the FAQ. Use the filter to switch between chapters. Community cards, by 5argon.

strings.landingnotice: Note: the Grimoire is updated in English first and translated into the other languages over time, so some content may take a while to reach yours. To see the very latest, check the English version. And if you have a Grimoire, FAQ or errata document you think is not on the site yet, email us at rinconmiskatonic@gmail.com and we will add it. Thank you!
strings.nobooknotice: Rincón Miskatonic has not been able to find up-to-date Grimoire or FAQ PDFs in your language. If you have them, please send them to rinconmiskatonic@gmail.com and we will add them. In the meantime, you can read the site in another language. Thank you!

strings.fmwarn: This diagram is NOT official: the community built it to break the timing down in far more detail than the rulebook does. It is carefully researched, but it may contain mistakes, and it never overrides the Grimoire or the FAQ. If you spot an error, write to us at {mail} and we will fix it.

strings.c1scopebody: The chapter 1 FAQ answers the products released BEFORE the 2026 Core Set, and applies to those products only. Some of its rules can contradict the Grimoire: when they do, the rule that governs is the one belonging to the product you are playing with.
strings.tour1d: This is the rules of Arkham Horror: The Card Game in a form you can actually consult: searchable, cross-linked, and in your language. Here is the gist, in five steps.
strings.tour2d: Pick your language here. Note that English always runs ahead: it is where updates are published first.
strings.tour3d: Seven visual themes, light and dark. Your choice is remembered in this browser.
strings.tour4d: The search covers both rulebooks at once, and tells you which one each result came from.
strings.tour5d: The sidebar holds the Grimoire (the 2026 rules) and the chapter 1 FAQ (the ones before it). They are different rulebooks and they can disagree: use the one that matches your product.
strings.tour6d: This site is a non-profit fan project, unaffiliated with Fantasy Flight Games or Asmodee. Enjoy your game!
